title: to ... (afraid to do) and preposition + -ing (afraid of -ing)
subtitle: afraid to do / afraid of doing
summary: Learn when an adjective is followed by to ... and when it is followed by a preposition + -ing, with afraid, interested and sorry.

lesson.heading: afraid to (do)
lesson.text: **I am afraid to do something** = I don't want to do it because it is dangerous or the result could be bad. So I don't do it.

examples.text: This part of town is dangerous. People are **afraid to walk** here at night.
examples.note: = they don't walk here at night because it is dangerous

examples.text: James was **afraid to tell** his parents what had happened.
examples.note: = he didn't tell them because he thought they would be angry

lesson.heading: afraid of (do)ing
lesson.text: **I am afraid of something happening** = I am afraid that something bad will happen. Here you are not choosing to do something or not - you are worried about a possible result.

examples.text: The path was icy, so we walked very carefully. We were **afraid of falling**.
examples.note: = we were afraid that we would fall

examples.text: I don't like dogs. I'm always **afraid of being** bitten.

lesson.note: So you are afraid to do something because you are afraid of something happening as a result: I was **afraid to go** near the dog because I was **afraid of being** bitten.

lesson.heading: interested in (do)ing and interested to (do)

left.label: interested in doing
left.text: = I'm thinking of doing it, I would like to do it.
examples: Let me know if you're **interested in joining** the club. (not to join)
I tried to sell my car, but nobody was **interested in buying** it. (not to buy)

right.label: interested to hear / see / know
right.text: = it was (or it would be) interesting for me.
examples: I was **interested to hear** that Tanya left her job.
I'll ask Mike for his opinion. I would be **interested to know** what he thinks.

lesson.note: This second structure is the same as surprised to ... / glad to ...: I was **surprised to hear** that Tanya left her job.

lesson.heading: sorry for ... and sorry to ...
lesson.text: We use **sorry for (do)ing** to apologise for something we have done. We use **sorry to ...** to say that we regret something that happens, and also to apologise at the time we do something.

examples.text: I'm **sorry for shouting** at you yesterday.
examples.note: you can also say: I'm sorry I shouted at you yesterday

examples.text: I'm **sorry to hear** that Nicky lost her job.
I've enjoyed my stay here. I'll be **sorry to leave**.
I'm **sorry to bother** you, but I need to ask you a question.

lesson.heading: to ... or preposition + -ing?
rows: I want **to do** it / I'd like **to do** it
lesson.note: After a preposition (of, in, from, on, to ...) we always use -ing, never to + infinitive.

lesson.text: Ask yourself: is there a preposition before the verb? If yes, use -ing. Note that in *looking forward to*, the *to* is a preposition, so we say *looking forward to going*.

exercises.prompt: The streets here are not safe at night, so a lot of people ___ out.
exercises.explanation: They don't go out because it is dangerous: afraid to + infinitive.

exercises.prompt: We walked very carefully along the icy path. We were ___.
exercises.explanation: We were afraid that we would fall, so: afraid of + -ing.

exercises.prompt: I thought she would be angry if I told her what had happened, so I was ___ her.
exercises.explanation: I didn't tell her because I thought the result would be bad: afraid to + infinitive.

exercises.statement: I don't like dogs. I'm always afraid to be bitten.
exercises.explanation: I'm always afraid of being bitten. We are afraid of something bad happening to us, so we use afraid of + -ing.

exercises.prompt: I don't usually carry my passport with me. I'm ___ it.
exercises.explanation: I'm afraid that I will lose it: afraid of + -ing.

exercises.prompt: If there's anything you want to know, you can ask me. Don't be ___.
exercises.explanation: Don't decide not to ask: afraid to + infinitive.

exercises.prompt: Let me know if you're ___ the club.
exercises.explanation: You would like to do it, so: interested in + -ing.
She is thinking of doing it: interested in + -ing.

exercises.prompt: I saw Joe recently. You'll be ___ that he's getting married soon.
exercises.explanation: It will be interesting for you to hear this news: interested to hear / know.

exercises.prompt: I'm ___ bad things about you. I didn't mean what I said.
exercises.explanation: You are apologising for something you did, so: sorry for + -ing.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.
exercises.answer: I was afraid to go near the dog because I was afraid of being bitten.
exercises.explanation: afraid to go = I didn't go; afraid of being bitten = I thought this bad thing would happen.

exercises.prompt: Which pattern follows each of these?
